evidence_items.explanation: The founding announcement pairs nonprofit research with freedom from financial-return obligations and encouragement to publish. Those commitments provide the baseline for assessing subsequent commercial and release practices.

evidence_items.publisher: OpenAI, Inc.; filing copy hosted by Gwern.net
evidence_items.locator: Certificate of Incorporation, Article THIRD, attached to California charitable registration
evidence_items.explanation: The certificate establishes public benefit and qualified openness as founding commitments. Its qualification prevents treating every decision to withhold a model as proof of a broken unconditional promise.

evidence_items.locator: FAQ: Why did OpenAI choose to release an API instead of open-sourcing the models?
evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI explicitly made commercial funding a reason to offer controlled API access instead of releasing the models. This supports departure from its original operating approach, while the same explanation also invokes accessibility and misuse prevention.

evidence_items.locator: About OpenAI, second economic and governance provision
evidence_items.explanation: The testimony records continuing nonprofit control and capped commercial returns; adjacent provisions require directors to further the public-benefit mission. This contradicts departure in the governance and beneficiary components, without proving that all conduct complied with them.

unresolved_gaps: The records do not establish whether restricted releases violated the founding qualification concerning when open sourcing was applicable.
Commercialization and restricted access do not themselves settle whether OpenAI ceased pursuing public benefit.
